## e6362765bc86

**Finding: base motifs are not guaranteed to identify a unique dihedral
transform.** The docstring says the base motif is asymmetric, but `_rand_motif`
only enforces non-empty/non-full density. A symmetric base can make multiple
transforms map panel 0 to panel 1, while those transforms produce different
answers on panel 2. The canonical rule then resolves the ambiguity only by its
hard-coded transform order.

Reproducer:

```text
generate(seed=1, sample_index=0, difficulty="easy")

panel 0 = 111   panel 1 = 100   panel 2 = 040
          001             100             000
          001             111             044
```

Both `rot180` and `transpose` map panel 0 exactly to panel 1, but on panel 2:

```text
rot180   -> 440 / 000 / 040
transpose-> 000 / 404 / 004
```

Thus the visible analogy is underdetermined even though the query distinguishes
the candidates. A model may learn the rule program’s transform-priority order
rather than infer a uniquely demonstrated geometric relation, and the declared
`transform` override is not necessarily the observable transform.

A future fix should reject any base motif for which more than one of the eight
dihedral transforms matches the selected panel-1 result. A stronger assertion
would require exactly one matching transform before accepting a sample. I did
not modify this audit target.
